readings.title: Yo'aḇ Besieges the Ammonite Capital
readings.subtitle: The Army Advances While Daviḏ Remains
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 20:1] And it came to be at the turn of the year, at the time sovereigns go out to battle, that Yo’aḇ led out the power of the army and destroyed <dn>את</dn> the land of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged <dn>את</dn> Rabbah. But Daviḏ remained at Yerushalayim. And Yo’aḇ struck <dn>את</dn> Rabbah and overthrew it.

readings.title: The Transfer of the Crown and Spoil
readings.subtitle: Extracting Wealth and Directing Terrestrial Labor
readings.text: [2] And Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> their sovereign’s crown from his head, and found it weighed a talent of gold, and there were precious stones in it. And it was set on Daviḏ’s head. And he also brought out <dn>את</dn> the spoil of the city, a very great amount. [3] And he brought out <dn>את</dn> the people who were in it, and put them to work with saws, and with iron picks, and with axes. And thus Daviḏ did to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then Daviḏ and all the people returned to Yerushalayim.

readings.title: Striking the Sons of the Giant
readings.subtitle: The Righteous Hedge Overcomes Physical Anomalies
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 20:4] And afterward it came to be that fighting broke out at Gezer with the Philistines. Then Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite struck <dn>את</dn> Sippai of the sons of the giant, and they were humbled. [5] And there was fighting again with the Philistines, and Elḥanan son of Ya’ir struck <dn>את</dn> Laḥmi the brother of Golyath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.

readings.title: The Fall of the Six-Fingered Giant
readings.subtitle: Daviḏ’s Servants Execute Authority Over Gath
readings.text: [6] And there was fighting again at Gath, where there was a man of great size, with twenty-four fingers and toes, six and six. And he too was born to the giant. [7] And he reproached Yisra’ěl, and Yehonathan son of Shim‛a, Daviḏ’s brother, struck him. [8] These were born to the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of Daviḏ and by the hand of his servants.

readings.title: The Covenant at Ḥeḇron
readings.subtitle: The Tribes Submit to the Appointed Shepherd
readings.text: [2 Samuel 5:1] And all the tribes of Yisra’ěl came to Daviḏ at Ḥeḇron and spoke, saying, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh. [2] “Formerly, when Sha’ul was sovereign over us, you were the one who led Yisra’ěl out and brought them in. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to you, <dq>‘Shepherd <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl, and be ruler over Yisra’ěl.’</dq> ” [3] And all the elders of Yisra’ěl came to the sovereign at Ḥeḇron, and Sovereign Daviḏ made a covenant with them at Ḥeḇron before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they anointed <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ sovereign over Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Chronology of Daviḏ’s Rule
readings.subtitle: Forty Years of Delegated Authority
readings.text: [4] Daviḏ was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years. [5] In Ḥeḇron he reigned over Yehuḏah seven years and six new moons, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years over all Yisra’ěl and Yehuḏah.

readings.title: Capturing the Stronghold of Tsiyon
readings.subtitle: Overcoming the Yeḇusites to Establish Daviḏ's City
readings.text: [2 Samuel 5:6] And the sovereign and his men went to Yerushalayim against the Yeḇusites, the inhabitants of the land. And they spoke to Daviḏ, saying, “Except you take away the blind and the lame, you are not going to come in here,” thinking, “Daviḏ is not going to come in here.” [7] But Daviḏ captured <dn>את</dn> the stronghold of Tsiyon, the City of Daviḏ. [8] And Daviḏ said on that day, “Anyone who strikes the Yeḇusites, let him go by the water-shaft and take the lame and the blind, who are hated by Daviḏ’s being.” That is why they say, “The blind and the lame do not come into the house.” [9] And Daviḏ dwelt in the stronghold, and called it the City of Daviḏ. And Daviḏ built all around from the Millo and inward. [10] And Daviḏ went on and became great, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts was with him.

readings.title: The Alliance with Ḥiram
readings.subtitle: Acknowledging YeHoVaH's Elevation of the Kingdom
readings.text: [2 Samuel 5:11] Now Ḥiram sovereign of Tsor sent messengers to Daviḏ, and cedar trees, and carpenters and masons. And they built a house for Daviḏ. [12] And Daviḏ knew that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had established him as sovereign over Yisra’ěl, and that <dn>He</dn> had exalted <dn>His</dn> reign, because of <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Offspring Born in Yerushalayim
readings.subtitle: Multiplying the Royal Lineage
readings.text: [13] And Daviḏ took more concubines and wives from Yerushalayim, after he had come from Ḥeḇron, and more sons and daughters were born to Daviḏ. [14] And these were the names of those born to him in Yerushalayim: Shammua, and Shoḇaḇ, and Nathan, and Shelomoh, [15] and Yiḇḥar, and Elishua, and Nepheḡ, and Yaphiya, [16] and Elishama, and Elyaḏa, and Eliphelet.

readings.title: The Master of Breakthroughs at Ba‛al Peratsim
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Shatters the Adversary's Forces
readings.text: [2 Samuel 5:17] And the Philistines heard that they had anointed <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ sovereign over Yisra’ěl, and all the Philistines went up to search for Daviḏ, but Daviḏ heard and went down to the stronghold. [18] And the Philistines came and spread themselves out in the Valley of Repha’im. [19] And Daviḏ inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Do I go up against the Philistines? Do <dn>You</dn> give them into my hand?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Daviḏ, <dq>“Go up, for <dn>I</dn> shall certainly give <dn>את</dn> the Philistines into your hand.”</dq> [20] And Daviḏ came to Ba‛al Peratsim, and Daviḏ struck them there. And he said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has broken through my enemies before me, like a breakthrough of water.” So he called the name of that place Ba‛al Peratsim. [21] And they left <dn>את</dn> their images there, and Daviḏ and his men took them away.

readings.title: The Divine Vanguard at the Mulberry Trees
readings.subtitle: Strict Adherence to YeHoVaH's Operational Strategy
readings.text: [22] And the Philistines again came up and were spread out in the Valley of Repha’im. [23] And when Daviḏ inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Do not go up, turn around behind them, and you shall come upon them in front of the mulberry trees.</dq> [24] <dq>“And it shall be, when you hear the sound of stepping in the tops of the mulberry trees, then act promptly, for then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall go out before you to strike <dn>את</dn> the camp of the Philistines.”</dq> [25] And Daviḏ did so, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded him, and smote <dn>את</dn> the Philistines from Geḇa as far as Gezer.

readings.title: Building the Royal House
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Establishes the Reign for Yisra’ěl's Sake
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 14:1] And Ḥiram sovereign of Tsor sent messengers to Daviḏ, and cedar trees, with stonemasons and carpenters, to build him a house. [2] And Daviḏ knew that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had established him as sovereign over Yisra’ěl, for his reign was highly exalted for the sake of <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Sons of Yerushalayim
readings.subtitle: The Multiplication of the Royal Seed
readings.text: [3] And Daviḏ took more wives in Yerushalayim, and Daviḏ brought forth more sons and daughters. [4] And these are the names of his children whom he had in Yerushalayim: Shammua and Shoḇaḇ, Nathan and Shelomoh, [5] and Yiḇḥar, and Elishua, and Elpelet, [6] and Noḡah, and Nepheḡ, and Yaphiya, [7] and Elishama, and Be‛elyaḏa, and Eliphelet.

readings.title: The Divine Breakthrough Against the Philistines
readings.subtitle: Elohim Strikes the Enemies by Daviḏ’s Hand
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 14:8] And when the Philistines heard that they had anointed <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ sovereign over all Yisra’ěl, all the Philistines went up to seek Daviḏ. And Daviḏ heard and went out against them. [9] And the Philistines came and made a raid on the Valley of Repha’im. [10] And Daviḏ inquired of <dn>Elohim</dn>, saying, “Do I go up against the Philistines? And shall <dn>You</dn> give them into my hand?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Go up, and <dn>I</dn> shall give them into your hand.”</dq> [11] And they went up to Ba‛al Peratsim, and Daviḏ struck them there. Then Daviḏ said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has broken through my enemies by my hand like a breakthrough of water.” So they called the name of that place Ba‛al Peratsim. [12] And they left <dn>את</dn> their mighty ones there, so Daviḏ commanded, and they were burned with fire.

readings.title: The Sound in the Tops of the Mulberry Trees
readings.subtitle: Deploying Elohim’s Heavenly Hosts to Battle
readings.text: [13] And the Philistines once again made a raid on the valley. [14] And Daviḏ again inquired of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“Do not go up after them. Go around them, and come upon them in front of the mulberry trees.</dq> [15] <dq>“And it shall be, when you hear a sound of stepping in the tops of the mulberry trees, then go out to battle, for <dn>Elohim</dn> shall go out before you to strike <dn>את</dn> the camp of the Philistines.”</dq> [16] And Daviḏ did as <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded him, and they struck <dn>את</dn> the army of the Philistines from Giḇ‛on as far as Gezer. [17] And the name of Daviḏ went out into all lands, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> put the dread of him upon all nations.

readings.subsection: The Genesis of the Davidic Dynasty
readings.title: The Six Sons Born in Ḥeḇron
readings.subtitle: The Early Years of Daviḏ's Governance
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 3:1] And these were the sons of Daviḏ who were born to him in Ḥeḇron: The first-born was Amnon, by Aḥino‛am the Yizre‛ělitess; the second, Dani’ěl, by Aḇiḡayil the Karmelitess; [2] the third, Aḇshalom son of Ma‛aḵah, the daughter of Talmai, sovereign of Geshur; the fourth, Aḏoniyah son of Ḥaggith; [3] the fifth, Shephatyah, by Aḇital; the sixth, Yithre‛am, by his wife Eḡlah. [4] Six were born to him in Ḥeḇron. And he reigned there seven years and six new moons, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years.

readings.subsection: The Genesis of the Davidic Dynasty
readings.title: The Descendants Established in Yerushalayim
readings.subtitle: The Exaltation of the Royal Family
readings.text: [5] And these were born to him in Yerushalayim: Shim‛a, and Shoḇaḇ, and Nathan, and Shelomoh – four by Bathshua the daughter of Ammi’ěl. [6] Yiḇḥar also, and Elishama, and Eliphelet, [7] and Noḡah, and Nepheḡ, and Yaphiya, [8] and Elishama, and Elyaḏa, and Eliphelet, nine, [9] all the sons of Daviḏ, besides the sons of the concubines, and Tamar their sister.

readings.title: The Lineage of the First Temple Sovereigns
readings.subtitle: Tracing the Authority to the Babylonian Exile
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 3:10] And Shelomoh’s son was Reḥaḇ‛am, Aḇiyah his son, Asa his son, Yehoshaphat his son, [11] Yoram his son, Aḥazyahu his son, Yo’ash his son, [12] Amatsyahu his son, Azaryah his son, Yotham his son, [13] Aḥaz his son, Ḥizqiyahu his son, Menashsheh his son, [14] Amon his son, Yoshiyahu his son. [15] And the sons of Yoshiyahu: Yoḥanan the first-born, the second Yehoyaqim, the third Tsiḏqiyahu, the fourth Shallum. [16] And the sons of Yehoyaqim: Yeḵonyah his son and Tsiḏqiyah his son.

readings.title: The Post-Exilic Royal House
readings.subtitle: Preserving the Seed of Promise Through Captivity
readings.text: [17] And the sons of Yeḵonyah the captive: She’alti’ěl his son, [18] and Malkiram, and Peḏayah, and Shenatstsar, Yeqamyah, Hoshama, and Neḏaḇyah. [19] And the sons of Peḏayah: Zerubbaḇel and Shim‛i. The sons of Zerubbaḇel: Meshullam, and Ḥananyah, and Shelomith their sister, [20] and Ḥashuḇah, and Ohel, and Bereḵyah, and Ḥasaḏyah, Yushaḇ-Ḥeseḏ, five. [21] And the sons of Ḥananyah: Pelatyah and Yeshayah, the sons of Rephayah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Oḇaḏyah, the sons of Sheḵanyah. [22] And the son of Sheḵanyah: Shemayah. The sons of Shemayah: Ḥattush, and Yiḡ’al, and Bariyaḥ, and Ne‛aryah, and Shaphat, six. [23] And the sons of Ne‛aryah: Elyo‛ěynai, and Ḥizqiyah, and Azriqam, three. [24] And the sons of Elyo‛ěynai: Hoḏavyah, and Elyashiḇ, and Pelayah, and Aqquḇ, and Yoḥanan, and Delayah, and Anani, seven.

readings.title: A Broken Heart's Acknowledgment of Transgression
readings.subtitle: Pleading for the Compassion of Elohim
readings.text: [Psalm 51:1] Show me favour, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, According to <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment; According to the greatness of <dn>Your</dn> compassion, Blot out my transgressions. [2] Wash me completely from my guilt, And cleanse me from my sin. [3] For I know my transgressions, And my sin is ever before me. [4] Against <dn>You</dn>, <dn>You</dn> alone, have I sinned, And done evil in <dn>Your</dn> eyes; That <dn>You</dn> might be proven right in <dn>Your</dn> words; Be clear when <dn>You</dn> judge. [5] See, I was brought forth in crookedness, And in sin my mother conceived me.

readings.title: The Purification of the Hidden Part
readings.subtitle: Restoring Wisdom and Total Cleansing
readings.text: [6] See, <dn>You</dn> have desired truth in the inward parts, And in the hidden part <dn>You</dn> make me know wisdom. [7] Cleanse me with hyssop, and I am clean; Wash me, and I am whiter than snow. [8] Let me hear joy and gladness, Let the bones <dn>You</dn> have crushed rejoice. [9] Hide <dn>Your</dn> face from my sins, And blot out all my crookednesses.

readings.title: The Request for True Atonement and the Ruach
readings.subtitle: Renewing a Steadfast Spirit to Teach the Way
readings.text: [Psalm 51:10] Create in me a clean heart, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, And renew a steadfast spirit within me. [11] Do not cast me away from <dn>Your</dn> presence, And do not take <dn>Your</dn> Set-apart Spirit from me. [12] Restore to me the joy of <dn>Your</dn> deliverance, And uphold me, Noble Spirit! [13] Let me teach transgressors <dn>Your</dn> ways, So that sinners turn back to <dn>You</dn>.

readings.title: The Sacrifice of a Crushed Spirit
readings.subtitle: Righteous Offerings From a Submissive Will
readings.text: [14] Deliver me from blood-guilt, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>Elohim</dn> of my deliverance, Let my tongue sing aloud of <dn>Your</dn> righteousness. [15] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, open my lips, And that my mouth declare <dn>Your</dn> praise. [16] For <dn>You</dn> do not desire slaughtering, or I would give it; <dn>You</dn> do not delight in ascending offering. [17] The slaughterings of <dn>Elohim</dn> are a broken spirit, A heart broken and crushed, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, These <dn>You</dn> do not despise. [18] Do good in <dn>Your</dn> good pleasure to Tsiyon; Build the walls of Yerushalayim. [19] Then <dn>You</dn> would delight in slaughterings of righteousness, In ascending offering and complete ascending offering; Then young bulls would be offered on <dn>Your</dn> slaughter-place.
